fit.gap_handling_summary: Gaps (Terragrunt, production cloud, mTLS, system design) are left out rather than faked; Terraform, AWS and Kubernetes are clearly qualified as personal/basic/namespace-level. The closest real experience is shown well.

issues: Headline puts 'DevOps / Platform Engineering' before the actual title and may be read as a current role
Projects partly repeat the Odrava experience bullets (pipeline speed-up, ephemeral environments, flaky dashboard)

ats.reason: Clean, well-ordered single-column text with standard headings; the candidate's real matches (Terraform, AWS, Kubernetes, TLS, Linux, monitoring) are all searchable and honestly qualified. The remaining gaps are skills she lacks.

issues: Company specificity is limited to the new train fleet and the ad's scope; values and engineering-led culture are not used
Does not address leading technical topics, stakeholder work or the contractor/B2B engagement
Closing paragraph is somewhat generic ('consequential infrastructure challenge')
strengths: Honest, clear framing of the Kubernetes and Terraform limits
No stale content from the earlier letter

spacing_issues: Lower third of CV page 2 is empty
consistency_issues: First job's dates sit on their own line under the title, while the other entries have right-aligned dates

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'to a consequential infrastructure challenge' is slightly stilted

notes_facts_used: CKA exam booked Jan 2027, not passed
namespace-level Kubernetes access; platform team runs the cluster
internal CI doc used in onboarding

requests.request: Please write my CV first, then the cover letter.
requests.evidence: Both a CV and a cover letter were produced

evaluation.summary: A truthful, well-structured tailoring for a career-switcher: the experience, metrics and homelab are presented accurately, and Terraform, AWS and Kubernetes limits are stated plainly in both documents. The ATS text is clean and shows every relevant skill the candidate really has. Weaknesses: a headline that leads with DevOps, duplicated projects and experience content, and a cover letter that skips leadership and stakeholder topics and uses little company culture. Real gaps (Terragrunt, production cloud, mTLS, system design) remain but are not faked.
